title: Honda and Toyota Recall 1.6 Million Vehicles. ICE Arrests Rattle a Flight. Mexico Nabs a Cartel Boss.
subject: Honda and Toyota Recall 1.6 Million Vehicles. ICE Arrests Rattle a Flight. Mexico Nabs a Cartel Boss.
preview_text: Check your airbags, arrests on a Seattle jet bridge, and a deadly raid in Sinaloa.
description: Honda and Toyota recall about 1.6 million vehicles, ICE arrests two people at a Seattle gate, and Kansas City wins the NWSL title.
contents_extra: How Mexico captured one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Honda and Toyota Recall About 1.6 Million Vehicles Over Takata Airbags

photo.alt: Steering wheel with an airbag cover; file photo.

paragraphs: Honda and Toyota are recalling about 1.6 million vehicles over a risk that Takata airbag inflators could rupture, Reuters reports via NBC News. Both automakers said no ruptures, crashes or injuries are tied to these vehicles.

Honda said it will recall 810,592 U.S. vehicles from model years 2012-2013 and replace the inflators for free. These inflators contain a moisture-absorbing desiccant, unlike earlier recalls. Honda said the recall covers vehicles sold or registered in 14 states and territories.

stories.title: ICE Arrests Two People on a Seattle Jet Bridge as Holiday Travel Ramps Up

photo.alt: Plane parked at an airport jet bridge; file photo.

paragraphs: Masked immigration officers detained two people on a crowded Seattle airport jet bridge on Saturday, the AP reports via NBC News. The Los Angeles-bound Alaska Airlines flight was delayed. Alaska said ICE gave no advance notice during a busy pre-Thanksgiving weekend.

DHS said the operation targeted a Mexican man who allegedly overstayed his visa, CBS News reports. ICE said a second passenger hurled hot coffee at officers and could be charged with assault. Gov. Bob Ferguson called the video horrific and chilling, ABC News reports.

stories.title: A Russian Strike Hits Kryvyi Rih as Drones Hit a Ship Near Finland

photo.alt: Apartment block with shattered windows; file photo.

paragraphs: A Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 60, local officials said Saturday, the AP reports via NBC News. A 7-year-old boy was among the dead. About 25 apartment buildings and a hospital were damaged, the city chief said.

A cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad was struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, Russian and Finnish authorities said. Reuters reports via NBC News that it caught fire and drifted into Finnish waters. Finland then tightened security in the area.

stories.title: The Kansas City Current Win Their First NWSL Championship

photo.alt: Soccer stadium lit up at night; file photo.

paragraphs: The Kansas City Current beat the Washington Spirit 2-1 on Saturday night for their first NWSL title, the AP reports via NBC News. Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly off a corner kick in the 54th minute.

Debinha added a goal deep in stoppage time, CBS News reports, and Trinity Rodman pulled one back for Washington in the 98th minute. Washington has lost in the final the last three seasons, the AP reports.

deep_dive.title: How Mexico Captured One of the FBI's Ten Most Wanted Fugitives

photo.alt: Military helicopter in flight; file photo.

paragraphs: What happened. Mexican forces captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro, the AP reports via NBC News. The firefight in Sinaloa state left at least 11 people dead. Mexico's Defense Ministry said seven alleged cartel gunmen and four soldiers were killed. He was flown to Mexico City on Saturday.

Why it matters. Meza Flores was one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives, ABC News reports. The U.S. had offered up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest. Authorities allege he leads the Beltran-Leyva organization, aligned with the Mayos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel. The AP calls his capture a blow to that cartel.

What each side says. Mexico's defense secretariat said elite agents were attacked with gunfire and explosives, CBS News reports. Mexico said intelligence from the Trump administration helped, but gave few details, the AP reports. The DEA commended Mexican authorities. Residents of Guasave were left terrorized by heavy gunfire and burning trucks, the AP says.

What comes next. Meza Flores and two lieutenants were placed with Mexico's organized crime prosecutors, CBS News reports. He is subject to a U.S. extradition warrant on drug conspiracy charges, the secretariat said. Violence spread in parts of Sinaloa as word of the operation spread. The cartel is also fighting a rival faction for control.

World view: Estonia will close its road crossings to Russia. Road crossings will shut on security grounds from Dec. 1 for at least six months, and Moscow warned of a response; Reuters reports via NBC News.
A candy factory fire kills at least three in Indonesia. Officials said Sunday that 36 workers were unaccounted for after the blaze near Jakarta; the AP reports via NBC News.
An Israeli strike hits a truck in Gaza. The Gaza Health Ministry said three people were killed, and Israel said it targeted Islamic Jihad militants; Reuters reports via NBC News.
COP31 deal hangs in the balance. A new draft came out Sunday, two days after the summit in Turkey was due to end; Al Jazeera reports.
Need to know: A former GOP staffer is indicted over a hoax. Prosecutors say Natalie Greene falsely reported being the target of a violent political attack in 2025; NBC News reports.
Several people are shot at a California party. The Tulare County Sheriff's Office said multiple victims were hurt in Strathmore on Saturday evening; ABC News reports.
ICE detains a Princeton Ph.D. student. Eva Yi Xie was arrested at Reagan National Airport, and her attorney disputes that she is in the U.S. illegally; NBC News reports.
GOP hopes fade for one more party-line bill. Republicans have less than two months before handing Congress to Democrats on Jan. 3; NBC News reports.
Money & markets: Anthropic slides after its record IPO. The stock opened at $111.50 on Thursday and closed Friday at $88.91 amid a tech selloff; CNBC reports.
Retirees face a Dec. 31 deadline. Missing a required minimum distribution can bring an IRS penalty of up to 25% of the amount owed; CNBC reports.
Warren Buffett quadruples his Thanksgiving gifts. He gave $5.5 billion in Berkshire shares to four family foundations this year; CNBC reports.
Long-haul first class ends at U.S. airlines. American Airlines flew its last international first-class cabin this week as business class grows; CNBC reports.
Future frontiers: Quantum computing eyes the power grid. Companies are testing grid optimization as a possible near-term use for the technology; CNBC reports.
Texas opens giant moon and Mars landscapes. A new Texas A&M space institute next to NASA's Johnson Space Center opened Friday; NBC News reports.
Downdetector logs its busiest week of the year. The outage-tracking site was busiest during a week that included a major Microsoft outage; NBC News reports.
Hackers target supermarket refrigerators. Attacks on cooling systems in European stores show how everyday equipment can be exposed; CNBC reports.
The score: Ohio State's playoff hopes end. The preseason No. 1 Buckeyes lost 31-28 at Nebraska on Saturday for their fourth loss; ESPN reports.
Navajo Stirling stays unbeaten. He knocked out former champion Jiri Prochazka in the second round in Doha, Qatar; ESPN reports.
Gabriela Fundora keeps her belts. The undisputed flyweight champion floored Jasmina Zapotoczna twice and won a lopsided decision Friday; ESPN reports.
NFL road teams are thriving. Ten weeks into the season, it has rarely been better to be the visiting team; NBC News reports.
Life & culture: Macaulay Culkin is set to return in a new Home Alone. NBC News confirmed a Disney sequel is in the works with Culkin back as Kevin McCallister; NBC News reports.
Jeweler Paolo Bulgari dies at 89. His family announced Saturday the death of the man who helped turn Bulgari into a global luxury brand; the AP reports via NBC News.
Princess Kate opens up in a documentary. A trailer for Heal, about her life since her 2024 cancer diagnosis, was released Saturday; the AP reports via NBC News.
Shoppers stock up on emergency supplies. Spending on preparedness products rose after recent tech outages, according to Consumer Edge data; CNBC reports.

trivia.question: How much reward money did the U.S. offer for information on Fausto Isidro Meza Flores?
trivia.explanation: B. Up to $5 million. ABC News reports the U.S. offered up to $5 million in 2017 for information leading to his arrest or conviction.
